category_title: Young students with EBD, ADHD, and ODD exhibiting noncompliance and disrobing behaviors
minimal_context: Axel is sitting in his individual work area being asked to complete a reading assignment by his teacher.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Axel, it is time to work on your reading assignment in your work area.

STUDENT: I don't want to read! It's too hard! (pushes the book away, looking angry)

TUTOR: You need to open the book and start reading the first page.

STUDENT: No! I'm not doing it! (kicks off his shoes)

TUTOR: Please put your shoes back on and look at your book.

STUDENT: (Screams a swear word, pulls off his socks, makes an obscene gesture, and throws the book out of the work area)

options.A: Allow the use of technology, such as computers or MP-3 players, when completing the reading assignment in his individual work area.
options.B: Have Axel participate in the same reading assignment as classmates but provide an alternative means for accessing the materials, such as an auditory version of the book.
options.C: Provide positive praise statements for demonstrating appropriate calm down behaviors, and then prompt Axel to point to the corresponding boxes on the calm down schedule.
options.D: Demonstrate understanding of his frustration and provide a couple more days of flexibility for him to complete the reading assignment in his individual work area.
